findings.summary: All six party members were exhausted and Camper Gavi retained an 11-HP Eelektrik.

resolution.observed: The bounded corrected suffix ended in an authoritative win after 22 certified actions.

findings.observed_fact: RAM and battle text verified the whiteout after 26 certified actions.
findings.strategic_judgment: The final Birdlaw faint was downstream; the earliest reusable causes were the missed free Fake Out turn and stale reserve accounting.

findings.summary: Fresh Croakatoa selected Mud Shot instead of guaranteed-flinch Fake Out, allowing Ponyta a second damaging reply and exhausting the Ponyta reserves.

resolution.observed: Fresh Fake Out executed with a PP decrement, Ponyta flinched, no enemy move occurred, and Croakatoa reached the next decision.

findings.observed_fact: The original certificate marked Fake Out unsafe; replay hash 1e6b205578ce603a verified Fake Out executed, Ponyta flinched, no enemy move occurred, and the next decision was reached.
findings.strategic_judgment: The scorer incorrectly charged next-turn damage to the flinch turn. Fresh, damaging Fake Out is immediate safe tempo unless verified ability mechanics block flinching.

findings.summary: Reserve accounting stayed static after assigned opponents fainted and failed to preserve Birdlaw as the answer to both Sunflora and Dustox.

resolution.observed: Dynamic defeated-species reserve accounting passed its unit regression and the corrected suffix ended in an authoritative win.

findings.observed_fact: The v26 suffix spent Birdlaw on Sunflora while the already-defeated Eelektrik still kept Croakatoa reserved; the v27 scorer reconstructs defeated species from verified transitions.
findings.strategic_judgment: A completed matchup must release its role, while a role covering multiple remaining targets must retain a penalty for spending its future coverage.

findings.summary: The Ponyta phase consumed Lildozer and Croakatoa and reduced Ohmnomnom to 10 HP before later reserves appeared.
findings.observed_fact: Lildozer was burned and fainted, Croakatoa took two replies and fainted, and Ohmnomnom finished Ponyta at 10 HP with burn.
findings.strategic_judgment: This attrition was materially worse than the corrected Fake Out prefix and explains the later lack of depth.

findings.summary: Sunflora then consumed Bugatti and Ohmnomnom, leaving Bushtank and Birdlaw to face Eelektrik alone.
findings.observed_fact: Bugatti landed two Bug Bites before fainting; burned Ohmnomnom dealt 7 damage before fainting; Birdlaw finished Sunflora.
findings.strategic_judgment: Each Pokémon acted, but the cumulative reserve deficit made the Eelektrik endgame unwinnable.

findings.summary: The loss used 26 actions and eight switches, but no immediate switch reversal or no-action voluntary relay occurred.
findings.observed_fact: Every voluntary entrant attacked before leaving or fainting; the problem was matchup allocation, not raw switch count.
findings.strategic_judgment: Do not add a blanket switch ban; preserve future matchup coverage and free tempo instead.
